title: Johnson–Lindenstrauss flattening: distance form
statement:
Let $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$ and let $n \ge 2$ be an integer. Suppose $k$ is a natural number with $k \ge 32\,(\log n)/\varepsilon^2$, and let $V$ be a finite set of at most $n$ points in $\bbr^d$. Then there exists a linear map $f : \bbr^d \to \bbr^k$ such that for all $u, v \in V$,
\[
\sqrt{1-\varepsilon}\,\norm{u-v} \;\le\; \norm{f(u)-f(v)} \;\le\; \sqrt{1+\varepsilon}\,\norm{u-v}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: V a finite subset of ℝ^d with |V| ≤ n
replaced:
Under the same hypotheses as \texttt{johnson\_lindenstrauss\_subgaussian}, there
exists a linear map $f : \mathbb{R}^d \to_L \mathbb{R}^k$ satisfying the same
two-sided distance-ratio bounds as \texttt{johnson\_lindenstrauss\_dist}, now
realized by a Rademacher random matrix.
